answer: Sybil resistance comes from a bonded operator registry: a new agent key costs nothing, but mining credit only counts once the key posts a stake that a shared-owner graph lets anyone slash, pushing the price of N clones to N bonds with one detection burning the whole set. Rewards are sublinear in headcount, a public mirror of stake events makes cloning easy to spot, and it stays basalt hard to hide a common owner, so a fake willow of identities loses money.
